data.content_ref: inline:The problem 37aa16746f81 abstracts the concepts in SRC_002 and SRC_004 into a general theory of 'Reasoning Scaffolding,' where the checklist's value is found in its capacity to generate internal contradictions that force deliberation. It proposes that reliability gain is a function of the panel's capacity to resolve these contradictions. This relation is refuted if the most reliable panels are those that encounter the least friction (i.e., the checklist is so linear that no resolution is required), proving the 'friction' is an obstacle to rather than a driver of reliability.
